card.front: Design lens rule #1: what beats a dashboard?

options.label: One card.
options.outcome: One card. One next step, small enough to start. The other eighteen wait their turn, unaccused. **The room gets quiet enough to think.**

options.label: A dashboard — see everything at once
options.outcome: The wall comes back, brighter. You read all nineteen. You read them again. **You do none of them.**

choice.prompt: What do you put on the wall?

card.text:
The next room is a wall of nineteen tasks. Each one glows. Each one is urgent. The wall hums like it *wants* you to read all of it.

VESPER dims the wall to one card. "The wall is not the work," it says. "The wall is the *fear* of the work."
card.title: The Card

card.front: 30009 vs 30014 — which page may show **rows** like `AAPL 10 @ 150`?

options.label: Only 30014.
options.outcome: You hold the row behind the door. The manifest *clicks* — one page, one reader, one reason. **"Good,"** says VESPER. "The board can have the count. The cabin can have the name."

options.label: 30009 — the hangar board
options.outcome: The row blooms across the public board — a name, a dose, a time. The Feed screenshots it before you can blink. **The door was there for a reason.**

door.text:
The corridor past the cryo bay is lined with doors, and every door has a manifest beside it. VESPER steers you to one marked **MEDICAL — DECK 3**.

A row of light hangs in the air: a name, a dose, a time. "The Feed wants it," VESPER says. "The hangar board would love it. The captain's page would *earn* it. Which page gets the row?"
door.title: The Door

echoes.text: The row is still on the public board. You can't unsee it; neither can the Feed.
The sim you didn't order is still running in the hangar. **It's learning.**
Somewhere in production, a tiny bot is writing test data into the real log.
The cryo alarm still follows you. The crew has a nickname for you now.
The launch order is warm in your hand. **Your name is on it.**
The stale task waits, unaccused. It will ask again.

end.ritual: Chapter Three opens when you're ready. Bring a washed face and a stretched back — **the reactor will need both**.
end.text: The door closes behind you and there is no handle on this side. **"Every door is a decision,"** VESPER says, "about who holds the pen." Somewhere below, the reactor *ticks*. Chapter Three: **the smallest unit is the blast radius.**
end.title: End of Chapter Two

card.front: A press would send a value. Where must the value come from?

options.label: The default — it was already filled in
options.outcome: You send the default. Somewhere below, a training sim you never asked for begins, and the hangar crew runs to a drill that has no instructor. **The form filed a fact you didn't choose.**

options.label: From her press — never from a default the card opened on.
options.outcome: You clear the form. The button goes dark until you choose a time, a crew, a reason. **"There,"** says VESPER, almost kindly. "Now it's a decision instead of a habit."

choice.prompt: Where does the value come from?

pen.text:
Inside, a launch order waits on a lectern. The form is already filled in: **TRAINING SIM, 06:00, CREW: ALL.** The cursor blinks beside a button that says *Send*.

"It opened on that," VESPER says. "It always opens on that. The question is whether *you* opened it."
pen.title: The Pen

options.label: A port number
options.outcome: You say "port 4222." The radio hisses. Every bot on the ship hears its own name and answers at once. **The Feed calls it 'the chorus.'**

options.label: A dotted name a message is sent to, like terrain.tip.today — domain, then noun, then verb.
options.outcome: You say **`terrain.tip.today`** — domain, noun, verb. The radio *clicks* and a single page on a single deck answers. **A channel, not a broadcast.**

radio.text:
The wall bot hands you a radio with no dial. "Say a name," it says. "Any name with dots."

A subject is how the ship hears you. Say it wrong and the message goes nowhere — or worse, everywhere.
radio.title: The Radio

card.front: Why do bots default to port **4223**, not 4222?

options.label: Fail-safe.
options.outcome: You point the bot at 4223. It salutes the empty sim and begins its rounds in a room with no stakes. **No bad data reaches the front line.**

options.label: 4222 — production is where the real work is
options.outcome: The bot marches into production and starts posting test rows into the live log. Nothing catches fire. **That's the problem.**

choice.prompt: Which port does the bot take?

sim.text:
A maintenance bot wakes in the wall and asks for a port. Two numbers glow: **4222** and **4223**.

"One of them is the front line," VESPER says. "One is the training sim. The bot doesn't know the difference. You do."
sim.title: The Sim

card.front: How does the system talk about a task that's gone stale?

options.label: Mark it overdue in red
options.outcome: The badge turns red. The wall leans in. You close the page — not because the task is done, but because **the page made you feel small.**

options.label: It asks "still true?" — never accuses.
options.outcome: You answer the question, not the accusation. The task stays or it goes. Either way, **nothing is added to the weight.**

choice.prompt: How do you ask about it?

stale.text:
One card is older than the others. It has been on the wall for months. You brace for the red badge, the streak, the small voice that says *you failed*.

Instead the card asks: **"Still true?"**
stale.title: Still True?

title: Chapter Two — The Door Decides the Row
